findings.title: Privacy notice lacks key UK GDPR transparency information
findings.detail: The supplied privacy notice identifies SJP and lists topics such as Google Analytics, cookies and overseas transfers, but does not state the applicable lawful bases, recipients or categories of recipients, retention periods, or the specific data-subject rights and complaint route. These omissions make it difficult for visitors to understand how information collected through the site is used and disclosed.
findings.reasoning: This is a significant transparency gap, but the evidence does not establish that every listed topic is absent from the full online policy beyond the supplied text. Medium is therefore more appropriate than high.

letter.subject: Concern regarding cookie and tracking practices on sjp.co.uk
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive privacy audit of https://sjp.co.uk on 2026-11-08 04:15 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit detected the cookie banner, clicked the reject option (“Decline All”), then recorded what was still sent while browsing the site.

The pages visited after rejection were:
1. https://www.sjp.co.uk/individuals/see-your-wealth-differently
2. https://www.sjp.co.uk/careers
3. https://www.sjp.co.uk/advisers

The privacy policy reviewed was:
1. https://www.sjp.co.uk/site-services/privacy-policy

The main issues identified were:
1. After cookies were rejected, Google still received data. We observed 63 requests to google-analytics.com, googlesyndication.com and googletagmanager.com after the “Decline All” option was clicked. This raises concern that advertising or other non-essential tracking may still be operating despite rejection.
2. Our automated review suggests that the privacy notice may lack key UK GDPR transparency information. While the notice identifies SJP and refers to topics including Google Analytics, cookies and overseas transfers, it appears not to state the applicable lawful bases, recipients or categories of recipients, retention periods, or the specific data subject rights and complaint route. This appears to make it difficult for visitors to understand how information collected through the site is used and disclosed.

Please would you:
1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies, trackers or similar technologies you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking that is set or activated without consent.
4. Confirm whether you intend to make any changes to the privacy notice in relation to the transparency points identified.

I would be grateful for your response within one month. If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit observed Google requests continuing after the cookie banner's rejection choice, including requests associated with advertising and analytics. The supplied policy text also provides insufficient detail on several UK GDPR transparency requirements, particularly lawful bases, recipients, retention and rights. The latter issue is rated medium because the supplied text may not represent every section available through the linked policy.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: True. Reject clicked successfully: True. Method: selector. Buttons clicked: Decline All.

E2: Tracker Google (Advertising): 15 requests before consent, 63 after reject, to google-analytics.com, googlesyndication.com, googletagmanager.com. Example after-reject requests: https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-W2ZFB5N&gtg_health=1 | https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-PLFT2V3&l=dataLayer
E3: Pages browsed and scrolled after reject: https://www.sjp.co.uk/individuals/see-your-wealth-differently, https://www.sjp.co.uk/careers, https://www.sjp.co.uk/advisers.
E4: Privacy policy: https://www.sjp.co.uk/site-services/privacy-policy. Companies it names: Google Analytics. Contact email found: None.

E6: Automated check (high): Google still received data after you rejected cookies. 63 requests to google-analytics.com, googlesyndication.com, googletagmanager.com after you clicked reject (Advertising).
